name: Riggs Hotel Washington DC
positioning: Hotel in the former Riggs National Bank building, constructed in 1891, on the corner of 9th and F Street in downtown D.C.
best_for: Travelers who want a downtown D.C. base in a historic bank building
Cocktail lovers curious about a bar set in the original bank vault

facts.text: The building was constructed in 1891 as a headquarters for Riggs National Bank.
The bank building was known as the Bank of Presidents.
The hotel is on the corner of 9th and F Street, in the former Riggs National Bank building.
The hotel is in downtown D.C.
Café Riggs is in the former bank tellers' hall.
Café Riggs has an ornate ceiling and original Corinthian columns.
Meeting and event spaces range from the rooftop to the Riggs Suite.
Through the LORE DISCOVERY loyalty program, members earn DISCOVERY Dollars on stays and in the hotel's bars and restaurants.

highlights.text: The guest rooms and suites are designed to be reminiscent of a private safety deposit box.
Silver Lyan, a bar in the building's original bank vault, is the first bar outside of Europe from Mr Lyan.
Moments throughout the hotel draw on a narrative inspired by the golden age of banking.

considerations.text: After 7 pm, Silver Lyan asks all guests to have valid 21+ IDs.
Silver Lyan recommends booking a table; walk-ins are taken first come, first served from a waitlist.
WhataHotel notes limited parking availability in the downtown location.
